review_asks.title: This wave's integration graph covers one application with no peer systems, no cross-app data flows, and one unowned external hyperlink dependency.
review_asks.why: States for the record what this synthesis pass found so downstream Rationalization and G-RR evidence review start from an accurate baseline.
review_asks.assessment: The wave contains a single application, 'Student Management System (VB.NET)' (c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9) — a standalone WinForms desktop CRUD tool over a local MS Access file with no network, API, batch, or messaging surface. No multi-subsystem decomposition fires (one tech-stack family, one top-level build directory, one build manifest). Because there is no peer application in scope, the graph records exactly one system node, an empty cross-app data_flows[], shared_identifiers[], and cross_system_capabilities[] (the last requires 2+ systems by schema), and one external_deps[] entry for the application's sole outbound reference: a hardcoded public GitHub link to the author's project-report PDF, which has no internal or external owner of record.
review_asks.reasoning: Derived directly from the per-app Discovery bundle: catalog.json (archetype, tech stack, business domain), structural-analysis.json (module map, coupling indicators, integration_points, interface-inventory), and call-graph.json (9 code-to-code edges, 7 code-to-data edges, 1 outbound edge — all internal to this single build target, none crossing to another registered application). No data-flow-tracer or identity-landscape artifacts were staged for this app, consistent with it being a simple, non-SSO, non-batch desktop tool.

review_asks.title: The dashboard's 'Report' button opens a hardcoded public GitHub URL with no internal owner — should this external reference survive migration, or be dropped as an unimplemented requirement?
review_asks.why: Nobody can decide whether to carry this dependency forward, replace it, or retire it until an owner (or a decision that it has none) is recorded, and it currently blocks closing out the application's only outbound integration.
review_asks.assessment: ext-github-project-report has no internal business owner and no external organizational owner — it is a hardcoded Process.Start call to a specific public GitHub file URL. Discovery's own structural-analysis explicitly recommends treating it as 'a requirements gap to confirm with stakeholders, not as an integration to migrate', since the button is labelled 'Report' but produces no actual report.
review_asks.reasoning: The call graph models this as the application's only outbound network edge (form1-dashboard -> external.github-project-report), and the interface-inventory lists it with audience='public' and authentication='none'. No CMDB, ownership, or ICD/MOU documentation was provided for it, and it does not match any entry a client external-dependency catalog would be expected to carry (it is not a partner-gov API, SaaS, or mainframe).

unresolved_references.finding: Single-application wave: this wave contains exactly one in-scope application (c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9), so there is no peer application to form a cross-app integration edge with. data_flows[], shared_identifiers[], and cross_system_capabilities[] are intentionally empty for this reason, not omitted in error.

GOVERNING-PROFILE DISCREPANCY (flagged by the input artifacts, not asserted here as fact). This task's governing client profile is declared as 'faa', but both the application catalog (catalog.json open_questions) and the structural-analysis pass (structural-analysis.json open_questions, 'GOVERNING-PROFILE DISCREPANCY') independently report that the in-scope application's source, README, and project report describe a generic single-developer student-record-management desktop tool with no aviation, NAS, air-traffic, certification, or FAA-adjacent content of any kind. This mapper does not adopt or restate any alternative governing profile; it records the upstream artifacts' discrepancy for the engagement owner to resolve before FAA-specific gating (safety tiering, NAS impact assessment, compliance mapping) consumes this graph.

No client-profile risk-classification.yaml or scoring.yaml was available in this workspace to derive systems[].tier, and the application's own safety_tier was left null by Discovery pending authoritative Safety Board / stakeholder input. tier is therefore omitted from the one systems[] entry rather than inferred.

Unprotected PII in source control: the committed studentDB.accdb (784 KB) holds live student personal data (name, father's name, two mobile numbers, DOB) with no database password and no application authentication, in what the structural-analysis pass identifies as a public GitHub repository. This is a data-protection finding orthogonal to integration mapping, carried forward here because it bears on whether/how this system's data store should be exposed in any future state architecture.
